p: The video demonstrates reviewing an AI-generated design doc via Artifact Share. A user highlights text to request a timeline reduction, prompts Claude via CLI to apply the feedback, and shows the updated document at the same URL with resolved comments.
Teams can review and comment on AI-generated docs, and the agent updates the artifact in-place at the same URL.

[{"timestamp":"00:01.00","observation":"Opening title presents the core workflow question over a blurred doc."},{"timestamp":"00:07.00","observation":"Comment modal opens directly on the doc snippet."},{"timestamp":"00:12.80","observation":"CLI view shows Claude applying review comments."},{"timestamp":"00:17.40","observation":"Document reloads with revised parameters and resolved thread."}]

The pacing clearly demonstrates the product loop of inline commenting and agent-driven doc revision. Text scaling is mostly readable, though terminal text is slightly dense. Visual transitions and UI interactions are coherent throughout.

p: ["brand identity (artifactshare.com, URL, logo) absent until the final card","sampled frames never show the stated hook line ('Your agent wrote the design doc...') so the opening beat isn't verifiable as scroll-stopping","dense small UI text in frames 0/1/3 requires reading, weak for a fast mobile scroll","'same URL, any agent' message isn't visually reinforced — no URL bar or multi-agent cue shown"]

The demo mechanics are legible and coherent: doc drafted by Claude, human leaves one inline comment, CLI agent applies it, doc republishes with a new decision — a genuinely concrete product story. But the product itself (Artifact Share, the shareable-URL mechanic) stays offscreen until the very last card, so for most of the runtime this reads as a generic doc-review tool rather than a branded product, hurting salience and hook impact. Visuals are clean, consistent, and free of artifacts, but text density in the mid frames works against a fast scroll-stopping open.
